title: Long BTC — Post-FOMC DXY Confirmation Trade; Conditional on Warsh Neutral
entry: CONDITIONAL — do NOT enter before 3:30 PM ET on June 17 (after the Warsh press conference at 2:30 PM ET). Entry fires only if BOTH conditions are met simultaneously: (1) Warsh June 17 press conference delivers neutral-to-balanced language — no explicit rate-hike signal for July, no 'actively considering a hike' framing — AND (2) DXY closes below 100 on the June 17 session. If both conditions are met, enter $65,000-68,000 in the June 17-18 post-presser window. Scale: 60% at first entry post-2:30 PM on June 17; 40% add on any $64,000-66,000 dip in the June 18-20 window. If DXY closes above 100 on June 17, do NOT enter — step aside and wait for the July FOMC.
stop_loss: $60,000 daily close — below the $62,000-64,000 institutional bid zone that the BlackRock Bitcoin Yield ETF has established, and below the psychological round number that BTC has repeatedly defended in 2026; implies DXY confirms above 100 for two consecutive sessions (Warsh hawkish signal fully priced), or BTC breaks the BlackRock ETF support bid, or macro risk-off re-accelerates on a June 17 close below SPX 7,460
targets: $72,000 — first psychological resistance above the $67K pre-Warsh ceiling; DXY confirmed below 100 for 3+ sessions; BlackRock Yield ETF institutional accumulation continues on the DXY relief; +8.6% from $66,287

catalyst: BTC is at $66,287 (June 16) supported by the BlackRock Bitcoin Yield ETF institutional bid, but held in a $64,000-67,000 range by the DXY at 99.57 — only 0.43 points below the 100 regime trigger. The June 17 FOMC at 2:30 PM ET (Warsh press conference) is the binary outcome. If Warsh is neutral-to-balanced, DXY likely falls from 99.57 toward 98.5-99.0 on a relief trade, breaking through the $67K BTC resistance ceiling. The conditional entry structure ensures this position is only deployed when the macro context is confirmed supportive, not as a directional bet before the event.
thesis:
BTC's 2026 trajectory has been shaped by two macro forces pulling in opposite directions: institutional demand (BlackRock Bitcoin Yield ETF, corporate treasury adoption, ETF inflows) and dollar strength (DXY above 100 on Iran-related uncertainty, Fed hawkishness). The Iran Islamabad Declaration on June 14 resolved the first headwind — oil is now below $76, removing the stagflation-driven Fed pressure that was the most acute BTC-negative macro signal. The remaining headwind is DXY/Fed, and the June 17 FOMC is the pivotal test.

BTC's correlation with DXY has been strongly negative in 2026, reflecting the macro dynamic: when the dollar strengthens on risk-off/Fed-hawkish signals, BTC sells off as risk appetite contracts; when the dollar weakens on risk-on/Fed-dovish signals, BTC rallies as institutional buyers rotate from dollar-denominated safe havens into crypto. The DXY at 99.57 has been the ceiling for BTC's $63,000-67,000 range: every time BTC approached $67,000-67,500, DXY was also testing 100, and institutional buyers paused. A Warsh neutral outcome that pushes DXY to 98.5-99.0 removes that ceiling cleanly.

The BlackRock Bitcoin Yield ETF is the structural support mechanism that distinguishes this BTC setup from the prior BTC long (long-btc-risk-on-liquidity-2026-05-21, stopped out at $61,000 in the May regime deterioration). The BlackRock ETF, which generates yield by lending BTC through institutional channels, has attracted approximately $4.2B in net inflows since its May 2026 launch. This is a different buyer profile from the retail-driven 2024-2025 cycles: yield-oriented institutions don't sell on 5-8% volatility the way retail buyers do. The $62,000-64,000 zone has held as a support floor through multiple macro headwinds precisely because these institutional buyers are not stop-loss-triggered.

The counter-party is the BTC bear who argues: (1) at $66,287, BTC is already pricing a neutral Warsh outcome — the conditional entry provides no edge if the base case is already in the price; (2) the DXY at 99.57 still has 30% probability of closing above 100 on FOMC day (market-implied); (3) CNN Fear & Greed at 40 (Fear) suggests retail BTC sentiment is already cautious, limiting the upside re-rating on a neutral outcome. The conditional structure (only enter post-Warsh with DXY confirmed below 100) addresses objection (2) directly — if DXY closes above 100, the entry never fires and the capital stays in cash.
bull_case: Warsh June 17 is neutral: 'We remain data-dependent; the current rate level is appropriate given the progress on inflation.' DXY falls from 99.57 to 98.2-98.8. SPX rallies to 7,580+. BTC breaks through $67,000 resistance within 2 hours of the presser and closes June 17 at $68,500-69,000. Entry conditions met; position initiated at $67,500-68,000. Over the following week, BlackRock ETF inflows accelerate as macro uncertainty resolves. BTC to $72,000 (Target 1) within 5 days.
bear_case: Warsh June 17 delivers a hawkish hold: 'We are actively monitoring upside risks to inflation; a rate increase remains on the table for July.' DXY closes at 100.2-100.4. BTC drops from $66,287 to $62,000-64,000 on the hawkish shock. Entry conditions NOT met — the position is not initiated. If DXY eventually closes below 100 after July FOMC, the entry zone re-activates but at a different price level. The conditional structure prevents a loss in the bear case.
invalidation: Entry conditions not met by June 20 (DXY above 100 on June 17 close); OR BTC falls below $60,000 before the entry fires (BlackRock bid broken); OR Warsh press conference contains explicit July rate-hike language; OR CNN Fear & Greed falls below 25 (Extreme Fear) indicating a broader risk-off environment that the institutional bid cannot offset

outcome.outcome_label: Entry condition 1 failed — Warsh sharply hawkish, not neutral
outcome.note: Entry required BOTH (1) Warsh June 17 neutral-to-balanced language AND (2) DXY closing below 100. Condition 2 was met (DXY 99.65). Condition 1 was the opposite of what was required: nine of 18 FOMC officials projected rate hikes, 2026 median rose to 3.8%, Warsh dropped forward guidance entirely and initiated a dot-plot review task force. The specific June 17-18 post-presser window has now permanently closed — the Warsh presser condition cannot be retroactively met. No trade was executed; return 0.0%.
